items.title: Fireworks allowed without permit on one night as Diwali celebrated in Mississauga
items.summary: City officials remind Mississauga residents of new fireworks rules as Diwali celebrations begin today and continue into early next week. This year’s religious and cultural festival takes place from Nov. 6-10, with the main celebratory day falling on Sunday, Nov. 8. “The City of Mississauga is reminding residents who plan to include fireworks in their celebrations to plan ahead, know the rules and put safety first,” city officials said in a notice to residents this week. Under the City of Mississauga’s relatively new fireworks bylaw, family/backyard fireworks can be used on private property with no permit needed from the city only on Nov. m. Fireworks cannot be used on roads, sidewalks, in parking lots or on other public property, the city added, noting a permit is required to use fireworks on another day (other than Nov. 8) or hold a fireworks display at a city park or public place. The city hopes to avoid a repeat of last year’s Diwali celebrations when it received the largest number of fireworks-related complaints in its history. The City of Mississauga received 432 public complaints related to Diwali fireworks celebrations in the days leading up to, on and after the 2025 Hindu festival of lights, which was held in October of last year. City officials said they’ll have extra bylaw enforcement officers on duty during Diwali to enforce rules and educate people on the proper use of fireworks. Residents are also being reminded not to call 911 about fireworks unless there is an immediate danger, such as a fire or injury. Illegal fireworks can be reported using the city’s 311 phone line or on the city’s website.

items.title: Closure: Crash closes all Highway 401 express lanes in Mississauga
items.summary: A crash closed all express lanes on Highway 401 in Mississauga on Friday morning. , according to the Ministry of Transportation’s 511 site. The Ontario Provincial Police said the lanes were closed at Creditview Road. MTO photos show a jackknifed truck and emergency crews on scene. The OPP is advising drivers to expect delays if travelling through the area, and to plan alternate routes if possible. items.title: Churchill Meadows Pool Back in Service After Sprinkler Leak Forced Months-Long Closure
items.summary: The indoor pool at Mississauga's $51-million Churchill Meadows Community Centre is back in regular use after an unexpected leak in the facility's sprinkler system forced an emergency closure at the end of summer, the city says. According to the City of Mississauga, crews have completed the repairs and reopened both the 25-metre, six-lane pool and the adjoining therapeutic pool. Drop-in swimming resumed earlier this week, and the city said regular registered programming is set to pick back up this Saturday. While the pool was shut down, aquatic programs were cancelled or shifted to other community centres nearby. The city acknowledged in its update that the closure created inconvenience for residents and added pressure on nearby facilities and staff. The community centre, which opened in late 2021 and also includes a triple gym and a teaching kitchen, sits on a 57-acre site on Ninth Line near Erin Centre Boulevard that includes Mattamy Sports Park.

items.title: Mississauga Changes Leaf Pickup Zones Ahead of This Fall's Vacuum Collection
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says its seasonal vacuum leaf pickup program is underway again this fall, though collection dates and zone boundaries have shifted for 2026. According to the city, the program is only available on streets that are more than 35 years old and lined with a significant number of large, mature trees, so not every neighbourhood qualifies. The city divides eligible areas into three colour-coded collection zones, yellow, blue and green, each with two scheduled pickup periods over the fall season. Officials are urging residents to check which zone their street falls under before raking leaves to the curb, since this year's zone map differs from previous years. The city said the program is meant to keep heavy leaf buildup off residential streets and out of storm drains as the season progresses.

items.title: $11M house with underground tunnel for sale in Mississauga
items.summary: An enormous home that’s become known as “Lorne Park’s Casa Loma” has hit the market in Mississauga. Today, Sam McDadi Real Estate Brokerage announced that one of the largest private residential landholdings in South Mississauga has gone on sale for the first time in its history. 5 acres and features some decidedly unique amenities–including an underground pedestrian tunnel. , was custom-designed by David Small Designs and built in 2005 on what was originally a vacant parcel. “While contemporary builds often prioritize minimalism, 530 Indian Road offers a distinct counterpoint in classical European architecture,” Ciro Napolitano, the listing’s sales representative with Sam McDadi Real Estate Brokerage, said in a statement. “The original owners built this home on a rare double-deep parcel in 2005 and poured artisanal detail into every square inch. From the double security gates to the underground tunnel leading to the pool house, it genuinely feels like Lorne Park’s private Casa Loma. ” According to the brokerage, which announced a record-breaking, multi-million-dollar home sale last month, the expansive property boasts an irregular 115-by-613-foot lot depth, which is not typically found in the upscale neighbourhood’s established grid. The eight-bedroom (three below grade), 11-washroom property’s Casa Loma comparison comes from its traditional European castle proportions, which includes Indiana-style cut stone, hand-carved classical columns, a multi-tiered front motor court fountain. The interior includes coffered ceilings, crown moulding, marble flooring, five natural gas fireplaces and a curved staircase. The house contains dual commercial kitchens, one with a walk-in refrigeration room. On the lower level, buyers will have access to an entertainment wing with a walk-in wine cellar, billiards hall, fitness centre, games lounge and guest quarters.

Drivers here pay premiums that are higher than in Burlington, which is the cheapest city for car insurance in the GTA at $2,109 per year. However, insurance costs in Mississauga are lower relative to the premiums in Brampton, the most expensive city in the region at $3,802 per year. The lowest average premium in Mississauga is found in the L5K area, where drivers pay $2,737 annually. Meanwhile, drivers in L4T have the highest average premiums at $3,937 per year. items.title: City Opens Its Downtown Model to Visitors for World Urbanism Day on Nov. 8
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is marking World Urbanism Day on Nov. 8 by inviting residents to explore the tools and resources planners use to shape the city's streets, parks and public spaces. According to the city, the Mississauga Civic Centre is open to the public and houses the Downtown Model, a miniature replica of the downtown core that shows how landmarks, buildings, streets and parks fit together, including Kariya Park and Square One. The city said planners consider how people move through the city and how roads, walkways and green spaces connect as neighbourhoods evolve over time. Officials are also inviting residents to a follow-up urban design open house on Nov. 19 to meet city planning staff and learn about the ongoing review of the city's urban design program. The city said the events are meant to give residents a better sense of the decisions behind the streets, parks and trails they use every day.

items.title: Third Suspect Named as Police Reveal Mississauga Arson Attacks Targeted Someone She Knew
items.summary: Peel Regional Police have named Madison Varga, 30, as the third suspect being sought in connection with two deliberately set fires at a Clarkson apartment building near Lakeshore Road West and Southdown Road. According to acting Det. Sgt. Natosha McBride, one of the two people already arrested in the case had a prior relationship with a resident of the building targeted in both fires. Police say the blazes were set in a third-floor hallway on Sept. 20 and again early the next morning, and investigators believe the same unit was deliberately targeted each time. Const. Laurie McCann told reporters at a Thursday news conference that one officer who responded to the scene suffered a hand injury that required surgery. No residents were seriously hurt, though 18 occupants of the seven-storey building were taken to hospital for smoke inhalation, and the second fire forced a large-scale evacuation that displaced several residents. Police estimate the two fires caused about $1 million in damage. Joshua Pedersen, 28, and Morgan Murphy, 27, both face arson-related charges, while Varga remains at large.

items.title: 2 arrested, police searching for suspect after Mississauga apartment building allegedly set on fire twice
items.summary: Two people have been arrested and police are searching for a third in connection with two fires they allege were deliberately set in September at a Mississauga apartment building.
